source.title: Open Problems in Engineering and Quality Assurance of Safety Critical Machine Learning Systems

accepted.question_text: How can a common, socially accepted quality-assurance framework be established for safety-critical machine-learning systems, such as automated-driving systems that rely on machine-learning or deep-learning models for environmental perception and decision-making, when there are not yet widely accepted quality-assurance concepts and techniques and when the relevant open problems must be organized across automobile standardization, statistics, software engineering, machine learning, and theoretical computer science?
accepted.context_brief: Standard QA framework for safety-critical ML

evidence.quote: Quality assurance frameworks are required for such machine-learning systems, but there are no widely accepted and established quality-assurance concepts and techniques. At the same time, open problems and the relevant technical fields are not organized.

Experts from each specialized field as mentioned in this paper should gather together, create technically reasonable drafts, proposing QA processes, and form consensus (standardization) overviewing the worldwide trends of safety-critical machine-learning systems.

accepted.question_text: How can safety-critical automated-driving systems define their operational design domain by efficiently collecting real-world driving scenarios from past field operational tests and customer data, and how can they define evaluation criteria such as test coverage to determine whether the collected scenarios are sufficient for safety and security assurance?

evidence.quote: Efficiently collecting driving scenarios on actual roads from past field operational tests and customer data remains a huge task and an open challenge in QA, but it is necessary for defining assumed environments and verifying the developed QA system against them. In addition, the evaluation criteria (such as test coverage) must be defined for the collected scenarios, in order to measure whether they are sufficient to ensure safety and security.

accepted.question_text: How can automated-driving system verification avoid infeasible field operational testing, which may require hundreds of thousands to hundreds of billions of miles, by using simulation and short-mileage test-course reproduction of rare corner-case scenarios that have extremely low occurrence probability on actual roads?
accepted.context_brief: Replacing infeasible FOT with scenario simulation

evidence.quote: However, obtaining statistically significant results would require conducting FOT by driving for hundreds of thousands to hundreds of billions of miles FOT [11]. In order to verify the system within a realistic time-frame, it is necessary to accelerate the experiment by simulation, reproducing the corner-case scenarios on test courses with a short mileage, i.e., scenarios with extremely low probability of occurrence and difficult to statistically obtain (rare) by FOT on the actual road.

accepted.question_text: How can developers describe the uncertainty introduced by machine-learning models inside safety-critical subsystems as statistical measures suitable for requirements, design, and assurance activities?

evidence.quote: Requirement: Subsystems with machine-learning models have uncertainty derived from the machine-learning models. Therefore, it is necessary to develop methods for describing this uncertainty as a statistical measure.

accepted.question_text: How can requirements for a safety-critical subsystem that contains machine-learning models be rigorously broken down into machine-learning-model requirements while combining deductive engineering with inductive machine-learning development and using safety-analysis approaches such as black-box verification, rule-based safeguarding, redundant and diverse architectures, and modification patterns that avoid the 'Change Anything Change Everything' principle?

evidence.quote: In fact, a subsystem should be subdivided and verified based on its development process, combining the conventional deductive approach with the inductive approach that is unique to machine learning [14]. Rigorous breakdown of subsystem requirements into machine-learning model requirements is essential for safety-critical machine-learning systems. In this process, safety analysis methods and processes are important, such as: black box verification; encapsulation of machine-learning models by rule-based safeguarding; redundant & diverse architecture that mitigates and absorbs the uncertainty of machine learning models; system modification patterns to cope with additional requirements without modification of the machine-learning model, in order to avoid the principle of CACE as much as possible.

accepted.question_text: Before expensive machine-learning model training, how can a redundant subsystem architecture be verified under a predetermined probabilistic uncertainty model so that engineers can know whether the uncertainty of the entire system is absorbed or mitigated?

evidence.quote: Moreover, in order to prevent reworking after training the machine-learning models, which is a heavy heuristic process, it is necessary to verify the validity of the redundant architecture. Assuming that a machine learning model behaves probabilistically based on the predetermined uncertainty, we would like to know if the uncertainty of the entire system is absorbed or mitigated, before training the model.

accepted.question_text: How should system-level assurance methods such as STAMP/STPA and Goal Structuring Notation be extended so that they can express uncertainty related to machine-learning models in safety-critical subsystems?
accepted.context_brief: Extending safety assurance notations for ML uncertainty

evidence.quote: System-level technologies STAMP/STPA [16] and GSN [17] have received attention in recent years. They are highly promising, but they will need an extension that can express the uncertainty related to the machine-learning models.

accepted.question_text: How can test-data requirements for a safety-critical machine-learning model be deductively designed from the future operational environment so that the test-data distribution reflects the operating conditions, the properties of the test data are described explicitly, and each assumed environment is associated with required model performance such as a condition-specific confusion matrix?

evidence.quote: Particularly in a safety-critical machine-learning system, it is necessary to design the test data distribution considering the operational environment, in which the system will actually be operated in the future, and to collect test data based on the designed data distribution.

However, the methods of describing the assumed environment of machine-learning models are not organized. In particular, we need methods to describe the properties of the test data. Furthermore, since the required performance may change depending on the assumed environment, it is necessary to express the association between the assumed environment and the required performance.

accepted.question_text: Which quality characteristics of machine-learning models, beyond accuracy or confusion matrices, should be defined and evaluated for safety-critical systems, including resource behavior, time behavior, robustness against adversarial examples, analyzability or interpretability, and testability for formal verification?

evidence.quote: In order to use machine-learning models in safety-critical systems, it is necessary to define and evaluate models by the performance indicators from various perspectives besides accuracy. If we refer to the software quality model [20], then accuracy (confusion matrix), resource behavior (required memory), time behavior (execution time), fault tolerance (robustness against Adversarial Examples [22], hereinafter referred to as AE), analyzability (ease of internal visualization or interpretability), and testability (simple model structure advantageous for formal verification) appear to be relevant perspective (performance indicator) to machine-learning models.

accepted.question_text: Because a trained machine-learning model's learned parameters cannot be manually specified or designed a priori, what information must be recorded, and by what process, to make the training of a safety-critical machine-learning model reproducible at least through its model structure, training data, training system, hyperparameters, initial parameters, and random seeds?

evidence.quote: Design: A machine-learning model is automatically obtained by training the model structure using the training data. Thus, specifications cannot be designed a priori. This limitation is essential, because high-performance machine-learning models are realized by learning high-dimensional parameters from data that engineers cannot manually specify.

However, in the development of a safety-critical machine-learning system, at a minimum, it is necessary to record the model structure, the training data, and the training system (including hyper parameters, initial parameters, random number seeds, etc.) to secure the reproducibility of the training process. In this way, specification is achieved indirectly.

accepted.question_text: How can operation and maintenance processes for safety-critical machine-learning systems continuously check consistency between current operational data and the originally assumed test-data distribution, and update or adapt models when operational data changes over time?

evidence.quote: Operational data tend to change with time, creating a major problem for the operation and maintenance of machine-learning models [21]. In this way, the deviation between test data used during development and operation data becomes large as time elapses from completion of development. It is important to check the consistency between the operational data and the test data (originally assumed environment), and to make the machine-learning models follow the operational data in a continuous maintenance process.

accepted.question_text: How can robustness against adversarial examples be measured for safety-critical machine-learning models when ordinary test data is insufficient, for example by generating perturbations near original test points and quantifying the largest adversarial examples for which the model still gives correct answers, and how can analogous measurement methods be created for other quality characteristics?
accepted.context_brief: Measuring robustness and non-test-data quality attributes

evidence.quote: Verification: Some quality characteristics cannot be evaluated with test data. For example, when evaluating robustness against AE as fault tolerance, it is necessary to artificially generate perturbations around the original test data points. We can generate AE near each individual test data point and quantify robustness by maximizing the AE to which the model can give correct answers. Besides robustness, there are also demands for measurement methods of various quality characteristics as listed above.

accepted.question_text: What concrete use cases can make interpretability and transparency methods for safety-critical machine-learning systems actionable, especially neural-network visualization methods that identify regions of interest through occlusion or activation back-propagation for debugging training and validating trained model behavior?
accepted.context_brief: Concrete interpretability and NN-visualization use cases

evidence.quote: Regarding interpretability, NN visualization [23] shows great promise. In NN visualization, one method intentionally performs occlusion on input data, and specifies the region where the inference result changes drastically as a region of interest; another method back-propagates activation values from the influencer nodes at the later feature extraction process to identify the region of interest. NN visualization may have use in cases of debugging during training, and validation of the training result (understanding the internal behavior of the trained NN). Therefore, one open problem is obtaining concrete use cases to address the interpretability and transparency of safety-critical machine-learning systems, by using NN visualization, interpretation, transparency methods.

accepted.question_text: How can automatic coverage verification based on formal verification technology be developed and applied to machine-learning models as part of quality assurance for safety-critical machine-learning systems?
accepted.context_brief: Formal coverage verification for ML models

evidence.quote: Furthermore, even in the field of theoretical computer science, toward a verification of machine-learning model, automatic coverage verification based on formal verification technology is becoming possible (Table 2). The technical areas necessary for QA at the machine-learning model level are machine learning and theoretical computer science.
